content.title: About
content.content: Peanuts are a legume whose seeds are commonly called nuts. Raw peanuts have a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a crunchy texture. They are eaten raw, roasted, boiled, and used in cooking to make pastes, sauces, and baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanuts belong to the legume family, not true nuts, and are more closely related to peas and beans.
Raw peanuts contain more protein than most nuts.
Peanut plants fix nitrogen, improving soil fertility.
Peanuts are used to make peanut butter, paste, milk, and flour.
Peanut flowers bloom above ground while the pods develop underground.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Peanuts provide about 25 % protein, making them a good source of plant‑based protein.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Most of the fat in peanuts is monounsaturated, which supports heart health.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High in magnesium and phosphorus
items.content: These minerals are important for bones, muscles, and nerve function.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Peanuts are one of the most common allergens; reactions can be severe.

items.title: Aflatoxin risk
items.content: Improper storage can lead to mold growth that produces aflatoxins, which are toxic.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Peanuts are calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Some people may experience gas or discomfort from raw legumes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw peanuts can be eaten as a snack, added to salads, oatmeal, yogurt, and used to make peanut butter, pastes, and baked goods. They are often roasted or soaked before consumption to improve digestibility.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw peanuts in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent mold growth and fat oxidation.
